content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary objective includes two populations but primary endpoint analysis only specifies SCC first",
      "quote": "To compare OS for patients with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer who have histology of squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and who have any eligible histology",
      "page": 37,
      "section": "2.1 Primary Objective",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary objective states OS will be compared in both SCC and any eligible histology, but the primary efficacy analysis section only describes testing in SCC patients first, with no explicit analysis for the overall population beyond a mention of higher power.",
      "fix": "Clarify the analysis for the overall population in the primary efficacy analysis section, including the testing procedure and estimand."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary endpoints lack explicit analysis methods for DOR and QOL",
      "quote": "Other secondary endpoints will include DOR and QOL. Duration of response will be defined as the time between the date of first response (CR or PR) to the date of the first documented tumor progression (per RECIST 1.1) or death due to any cause. Quality of life will be measured by the EORTC QLQ-C30.",
      "page": 43,
      "section": "4.2.3 Other Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The endpoints DOR and QOL are defined but no statistical analysis methods are described for them in the statistical plan (Section 10).",
      "fix": "Add analysis methods for DOR (e.g., Kaplan-Meier, Cox model) and QOL (e.g., mixed model for repeated measures, handling of missing data)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory endpoints lack analysis methods",
      "quote": "To measure concentrations of cemiplimab in serum and characterize the pharmacokinetics (PK) of cemiplimab",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.3 Exploratory Objectives",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Exploratory objectives (PK, immunogenicity, biomarkers, pharmacodynamics) are listed but no statistical analysis methods are provided in the statistical plan.",
      "fix": "Include analysis methods for PK, immunogenicity, biomarker, and pharmacodynamic endpoints in the SAP."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint is OS, defined as the time from randomization to the date of death. A patient who has not died will be censored at the last known date of contact.",
      "page": 43,
      "section": "4.2.1 Primary Endpoint",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The estimand for OS lacks explicit specification of the population (SCC vs all), variable (time to death), intercurrent events (e.g., subsequent therapy), and summary measure (hazard ratio).",
      "fix": "Define the estimand for OS with all attributes: population, variable, intercurrent event handling, and summary measure."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size section has incomplete sentence and missing inputs",
      "quote": "Two interim efficacy analyses are planned using Lan-DeMets (O’Brien-Fleming) spending patients will yield approximately 80% power to detect an HR of 0.7 with an overall type I error of number of OS events are provided in Section 10.5.",
      "page": 94,
      "section": "10.2 Justification of Sample Size",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The sentence is garbled and missing key sample size inputs: the overall type I error rate, the number of OS events, and the power statement is incomplete.",
      "fix": "Rewrite the sentence to clearly state the type I error, power, and number of events, and ensure Section 10.5 provides the event numbers."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of missing data for efficacy endpoints",
      "quote": "Data collected regarding the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the patients will be summarized (eg, discontinuation due to COVID-19). Any additional analyses and methods required to investigate the impact of COVID-19 on the efficacy (eg, missing data due to COVID-19) and safety evaluation will be specified in the SAP.",
      "page": 93,
      "section": "10 Statistical Plan",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical plan does not describe general missing data handling for primary or secondary endpoints, only defers to SAP for COVID-19 related missing data.",
      "fix": "Add a section on missing data handling for all efficacy endpoints, including censoring rules and sensitivity analyses."
    },
    {
      "title": "Multiplicity control for secondary endpoints not specified",
      "quote": "The key secondary endpoints are PFS and ORR.",
      "page": 43,
      "section": "4.2.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "No method for controlling type I error across multiple secondary endpoints (PFS, ORR, DOR, QOL) is described.",
      "fix": "Specify a hierarchical testing procedure or other multiplicity adjustment for secondary endpoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent definition of ORR denominator",
      "quote": "Overall response rate will be defined as the number of patients with a best overall response of confirmed CR or PR divided by the number of patients in the efficacy analysis set.",
      "page": 43,
      "section": "4.2.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The efficacy analysis set is defined as FAS (all randomized) in Section 10.3.1, but the ORR denominator may be ambiguous if some patients are not evaluable; also, the analysis set for ORR is not explicitly stated in the statistical methods.",
      "fix": "Clarify the analysis set for ORR and whether patients without measurable disease are excluded."
    }
  ]
}
